title: picocli-spec command spec
description: The JSON format read and written by picocli.spec.CommandSpecJson: describes a picocli CommandSpec (a command's options and positional parameters, plus any nested subcommands) without an annotated Java class. Compiling picocli.spec.CommandSpecDsl's DSL produces a CommandSpec that serializes to exactly this shape. Note: this schema is intentionally a little stricter than CommandSpecJson.read() itself, to help editors/validators catch likely mistakes -- see the two 'Stricter than the reader' notes below. Versioning: this $id is the unversioned URL and always reflects the latest release; each release also publishes an exact, permanently-kept copy at .../spec/schema/<picocli-spec version>/command-spec.schema.json (pin to that one for reproducibility).

$schema.description: Optional editor-validation hint (the conventional key many JSON tools add/read for autocomplete, e.g. pointing at this very schema's $id). Ignored by CommandSpecJson.read() and emitted at the root of generated JSON by CommandSpecJson.write().

name.description: The command's name. Optional at the document root (an unnamed root keeps picocli's own default); required on every entry inside "subcommands", since CommandSpecMerger and ordinary use both need it to address the subcommand.

helpSection.description: Optional help section tag for this command (e.g. "experimental"). Tagged commands are excluded from the parent command's standard usage help and rendered only when the matching help section is requested on demand.

helpSections.description: Optional definitions of on-demand help section metadata (headings, description lines, empty messages, notices).

mixinStandardHelpOptions.description: Sets whether the standard help options (-h, --help and -V, --version) should be mixed in with this command. Equivalent to picocli's @Command(mixinStandardHelpOptions = true).

argGroups.description: Each entry's own options/positionalParams (and any nested subgroups' args, recursively) are still visible on this command's own options()/positionalParameters() -- picocli's CommandSpec#addArgGroup registers them automatically. They do NOT also appear in this command's own "options"/"positionalParams" arrays; CommandSpecJson.write() excludes any arg that belongs to a group from those flat arrays specifically to avoid emitting it twice.

use.description: Names of definitions.bundles entries to expand into this command's own options/positionalParams (and any groups the bundle itself declares), in addition to whatever this command's own "options"/"positionalParams"/"argGroups" already list.

definitions.description: Named option/positional-param templates that this document's options/positionalParams arrays can reference by (string) name instead of inlining, reducing duplication when many commands share the same option. Only valid at the DOCUMENT ROOT: CommandSpecJson.read() rejects a nested "definitions" on a subcommand object, and "namedCommand" below forbids one for the same reason.

options.description: Keyed by whatever name a reference will use (conventionally the option's own long name, e.g. "--json"), but the key need not equal one of the option's own "names".

positionalParams.description: Keyed by whatever label a reference will use (conventionally the positional's own bare label before angle-bracket wrapping, e.g. "files").

bundles.description: Named, reusable bundles of already-defined options/positionals (and/or inline groups), expandable into any command's or group's own body via a "use" array entry naming one. A bundle may itself "use" an earlier bundle in this same map.

options.description: Names of options already declared in definitions.options that this bundle expands to -- always a plain name reference here, never an inline option object.

positionalParams.description: Labels of positional params already declared in definitions.positionalParams -- always a plain label reference here, never an inline object.

groups.description: Groups declared inline within this bundle, materialized fresh (with fresh option/positional instances) each time the bundle is "use"d.

use.description: Names of other definitions.bundles entries to fold into this bundle -- must already appear earlier in the same bundles map.

definitionReference.description: A reference to a same-named entry in the document root's definitions.options or definitions.positionalParams, instead of a full inline object.

exclusive.description: true (picocli's own default): at most "multiplicity" of this group's own args (not counting subgroups) may be matched together -- e.g. only one of a set of mutually-exclusive options. false: the group's args may all be matched together (still subject to their own individual required/arity), used to validate a co-occurring set as a unit (e.g. "multiplicity=1" cooperative group requires the whole set together, or none of it).

multiplicity.description: How many times this group as a whole may/must be matched. Parsed by picocli.CommandLine.Model.Range.valueOf(String), same format as an arg's "arity". "1" makes the group required.

heading.description: Usage-help section heading for this group.

hidden.description: This group is never actually built as an ArgGroupSpec: with "hidden": true, all of its members (and any subgroups' members, recursively) are instead flattened directly into the enclosing command/group, with each member's own "hidden" forced true. Verified empirically that a group whose every member is hidden otherwise still leaves visible usage-help artifacts (an orphaned heading, and a stray empty "[]" in the synopsis) -- flattening avoids that entirely. "exclusive"/"multiplicity"/"heading" are moot when "hidden" is true: no mutual-exclusion/multiplicity validation is performed for a hidden group's former members.

helpSection.description: Tags this group with a custom help section name (e.g. "experimental"). Tagged groups are omitted from standard --help usage messages, while their members remain visible to shell autocompletion. Rendered on demand when a matching trigger option is invoked.

use.description: Names of definitions.bundles entries to expand into this group's own options/positionalParams/subgroups, in addition to whatever this group's own arrays already list.

subgroups.description: Nested groups, e.g. a cooperative group containing two mutually-exclusive subgroups.

namedCommand.description: Stricter than the reader: CommandSpecJson.read() does not actually reject an unnamed subcommand entry (it falls back to picocli's placeholder command name), but that is almost always a mistake. A nested "definitions" block is forbidden here and the reader rejects it too: definitions are only read at the document root.

names.description: One or more option names, e.g. ["-v", "--verbose"].

usageHelp.description: Marks this as picocli's built-in usage-help option: matching it auto-prints the usage message and short-circuits execution (CommandLine#execute returns before running any Runnable/Callable). Options only -- picocli has no positional-parameter equivalent.

versionHelp.description: Marks this as picocli's built-in version-help option: matching it auto-prints the version message and short-circuits execution. Options only.

hidden.description: Excludes this option from default usage help while it remains fully functional. See CommandLine.Model.ArgSpec#hidden().

helpSection.description: Designates this option as an on-demand help trigger for the named help section (e.g. "experimental"). Automatically implies usageHelp = true.

paramLabel.description: Defaults to "PARAM" (picocli's own default) if omitted.

hidden.description: Excludes this positional param from default usage help while it remains fully functional. See CommandLine.Model.ArgSpec#hidden().

helpSection.description: Optional help section tag for this positional parameter (e.g. "experimental"). Tagged positional parameters are excluded from standard usage help and rendered only when the matching help section is requested on demand.

name.description: The section name/tag matching helpSection attributes on options, positional parameters, or subcommands.

heading.description: Heading displayed above the section when rendered on demand.

emptyMessage.description: Fallback message displayed when no elements in this section are present.

notice.description: Custom notice displayed in standard usage help pointing to this section.

type.description: See picocli.spec.ArgTypes. One of the scalar type names, optionally suffixed with "[]" for a multi-value array type -- required whenever arity allows more than one value: picocli can only bind multiple matches to an array or Collection type (Collection/Map types, which need an explicit auxiliary type due to generics erasure, are not yet supported; arrays cover the same need).

defaultValue.description: Applied as the default when the option/positional is not matched on the command line. Stricter than the reader: CommandSpecJson.read() actually accepts any JSON scalar here (numbers, booleans) and stringifies it, but a JSON string is the documented, forward-compatible contract. Note picocli itself reports an argument as not required (ArgSpec#required()) whenever it has a default value, regardless of the "required" field below.

arity.description: Parsed by picocli.CommandLine.Model.Range.valueOf(String): a single count, or a min..max range where max may be "*" for unbounded.

scope.description: "inherit" (picocli's ScopeType.INHERIT) makes this option/positional param also apply to every descendant subcommand, not just the command it's declared on. Omit (or "local") for the default, command-only behavior.
